title: FRCS (Glasg) Internal & Emergency Medicine Mastery
summary: An exhaustive clinical protocol guide for Acute Renal Failure, poisoning, burns, hypothermia, and perioperative management for ophthalmic surgical candidates. Designed for high-stakes exam preparation and emergency reference.

branches: Definition: Characterized by increased serum creatinine & urea, often with oliguria or anuria
Prerenal/Systemic: Hypovolaemia, low COP, Hepatorenal syndrome

sections.title: ARF Initial Management & Monitoring
content: 1. Catheterize: Assess hourly urine output & establish fluid charts.
2. Assess Intravascular Volume: BP, JVP, skin turgor, fluid balance sheet, weight, CVP.
3. Cardiac Monitoring: Attach to cardiac monitor.
4. Access: Consider inserting a central venous cannula.

sections.title: Comprehensive ARF Investigations
content: Blood: U&E, Ca2+, PO4-3, FBC, ESR, CRP, INR, LFT, CK, LDH, protein electrophoresis, hepatitis serology
Autoantibodies: ANA, ANCA, complement, anti-GBM, ASOT
Cultures: Blood cultures, Urgent urine microscopy & cultures
Urine WBCs: Infection & interstitial nephritis
Urine RBCs: Inflammatory glomerular condition
Imaging: USS of renal tract (exclude obstruction), ECG, CXR

sections.title: Hyperkalaemia: Red Alert (K+ > 6mmol/L)
content: Causes: Oliguric renal failure, metabolic acidosis (DM) & K+ sparing diuretics
ECG Sign 1: Tall T waves ± flat P waves ± increased PR interval
ECG Sign 2: Widening of QRS complex leads to VF/VT
TREATMENT: 10 mL Ca gluconate (10%) IV over 2min (Cardioprotection/threshold potential; NO change to K+ levels)
TREATMENT: Insulin (10U) + 50% glucose (50mL) IV over 30 mins (Moves K+ into cells)
TREATMENT: Nebulized salbutamol (2.5 mg) (Moves K+ into cells)
TREATMENT: Polystyrene sulfonate resin (Ca Resonium 15g/6-8h PO or 30g enema) to remove K+ from colon
TREATMENT: Dialysis

rows: 20 mL + previous hour’s urine output per hour
Urgent dialysis. Nitrate infusion, furosemide, 'renal dose' dopamine

sections.title: Urgent Dialysis Indications & Nephrotoxins
content: AVOID: Nephrotoxic drugs e.g., NSAIDS & aminoglycosides
DIALYSE IF: Persistent hyperkalaemia (> 6 mmol/L)
DIALYSE IF: Acidosis (pH < 7.2)
DIALYSE IF: Hypercatabolic renal failure
DIALYSE IF: Pulmonary edema & no substantial diuresis
DIALYSE IF: Pericarditis (in tamponade, dialyse after pressure relief)

sections.title: Acute Poisoning: General Management
content: A: Adequate ventilation
B: Oxygenation
C: Circulation -> IV line
D: Level of consciousness (Naloxone if decreased)
Monitor: Vital signs monitoring
Assess: History (patient/friends/family) + Physical examination
Investigate: Glucose, U&E, FBC, LFT, INR, ABG, ECG, Paracetamol/Salicylate levels, Toxicology

rows: Rarely used; Worse after 30-60m; Contraindicated: Petroleum/corrosives, unconscious, unable to protect airway. NEVER induce vomiting.
50g with water. Use for: Salicylates, paracetamol. Don't use: Petroleum, corrosives, alcohols, metal salts.

sections.title: Salicylate Poisoning
content: Dose: Mild (150 mg/kg), Moderate (250 mg/kg), Severe (>500 mg/kg)
Symptoms: Vomiting, dehydration, hyperventilation, tinnitus, vertigo, sweating
Rare/Severe: Coma, seizures, decreased BP, Heart block, pulmonary oedema, hyperthermia
Acid-Base: Respiratory alkalosis (central stimulation) then metabolic acidosis
Management: Gastric lavage (within 1h) + charcoal; Correct metabolic acidosis with HCO3 (Aim urine pH 7.5-8.5)
Dialysis: If salicylate level > 700 mg/L

sections.title: Paracetamol Poisoning & NAC Protocol
content: Threshold: 150 mg/kg or 12g (fatal). Symptoms: RUQ pain, jaundice, encephalopathy, renal failure.
NAC Step 1: 150 mg/kg IVI in 200 mL 5% dextrose over 15 min.
NAC Step 2: 50 mg/kg in 500 mL 5% dextrose over 4h.
NAC Step 3: 100 mg/kg every 16h in 1L 5% dextrose.
Alternative: Methionine 2.5g/4h PO for 16h (if NAC unavailable).
Specialist Transfer: INR > 2 (<48h) or > 3.5 (<72h), Encephalopathy, Creatinine > 200 umol/L, Blood pH < 7.3, Systolic BP < 80mmHg.

rows: Partial: Blisters, erythema, wet, VERY painful (epidermis/superficial dermis)
Full: White/black eschar, dry, PAINLESS (loss of nerve endings)
Serious Sites: Face/Neck (Oedema of glottis), Perineum (nursing difficulty)

content.explanation: 4 X weight (kg) X % burn = mL crystalloid solution in 24h (Half given in first 8h). Muir & Barclay Formula (Colloid/Albumin): [weight (kg) X % burn] / 2 per time period.

sections.title: Burns Management Process
content: Airway: Intubate if airway obstruction or smoke inhalation.
Breathing: 100% O2; exclude tension pneumothorax & CO poisoning (cherry-red skin).
Circulation: 2 large-bore (14 or 16G) IV lines.
Target Output: 0.5mL/kg/h (1mL/kg/h in children).
Cooling: Use saline/tap water but warm the patient to prevent shock.
Meds: Antitetanic/Anti-gas gangrene serum, antibiotics, morphine 10mg.
Dressings: Biological/Synthetic for Partial; Tangential excision/grafts for Full.

sections.title: Hypothermia Management
content: Definition: Core (rectal) temperature < 35º C.
Causes Young: Exposure, near-drowning, alcohol/drug overdose.
Causes Elderly: Impaired homeostasis, immobility, hypothyroidism, DM, confusion, drugs (tranquilizers, diuretics).
Investigations: U&E, glucose, TFTs, FBC, ECG (J-waves).
Management: ABCs, warm IVI, Urinary catheter, Antibiotics (if >65y and T<32C).
Rewarming: Slowly (Aim 0.5ºC/h). Rapid warming = decreased BP/shock.
Complications: Arrhythmias, pneumonia, pancreatitis, ARF, intravascular coagulation.
Prognosis: Age > 70y & T < 32C = Mortality > 50%.

sections.title: Needle-stick: Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP)
content: Immediate: Encourage bleeding, wash under running water; eyes: irrigate copiously.
Reporting: Within 1h to Occupational Health or A&E.
PEP Initiation: Within 1h for High Risk (sharps injury from known/suspected HIV donor).
PEP Regimen: Zidovudine 250mg 2x/d + Lamivudine 150mg 2x/d + Indinavir 800mg 3x/d.
Duration: Continue PEP for 4 weeks if donor is HIV+.
Testing: Recipient tested at 6 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months.

sections.title: Perioperative Contraindications (Ophthalmic)
content: Uncontrolled BP (>180/100 mmHg)
Myocardial Ischemia/MI within last 3 months
Uncontrolled Hyperglycemia
Uncontrolled Arrhythmias
Excessive INR
Acute Systemic Illness

rows: Continue antihypertensives (including day of surgery); Postpone if BP >180/100.
Continue antianginals; ensure sublingual nitro is available; postpone if MI < 3 months.
Antibiotic prophylaxis NOT required for intraocular procedures.
Continue for intraocular/strabismus; discontinue 2 weeks for orbital/oculoplastic (discuss with PCP).
INR < 3 for intraocular/strabismus; INR < 2 for orbital/oculoplastic. Check within 48h.

sections.title: Diabetic Surgery: Type 1 IDDM
content: Priority: Place first on the surgery list.
Insulin: Stop all long-acting insulin the night before. Morning of surgery: Stop all SC insulin.
Infusion: Start IV 1L 5% dextrose + 20mmol KCl/8h.
Pump: 50U short-acting insulin in 50mL 0.9% saline per sliding scale.
Monitoring: Check blood glucose hourly; aim for 7-11mmol/L during surgery.
Post-op: Continue IV insulin/dextrose until tolerating food.

sections.title: Diabetic Surgery: Type 2 NIDDM
content: Control: If fasting glucose > 10mmol/L, treat as Type 1.
Sulphonylureas: Do not give long-acting (e.g., glibenclamide) on morning of surgery (risk of prolonged hypoglycemia).
Metformin: Beware lactic acidosis, especially with IV contrast or poor renal function (Creatinine > 150 umol/L).
Major Surgery: Check fasting glucose; start IV/SC insulin sliding scale if NBM post-op.

sections.title: Local Anaesthetic (LA) Toxicity
content: Signs: Sudden LOC ± tonic-clonic convulsions; Cardiovascular collapse (Bradycardia, conduction blocks, asystole, VT).
Immediate: STOP injection, call for help, maintain airway/100% O2, confirm IV access.
Seizures: Small incremental doses of benzodiazepine, thiopental, or propofol.
Cardiac Arrest CPR: Start standard CPR; manage arrhythmias; consider bypass.
LIPID EMULSION (70kg patient): IV Bolus Intralipid 20% 1.5 ml/kg (100ml) over 1 min.
INFUSION: Start Intralipid at 0.25 ml/kg/min (400ml over 20 min).
REFRACTORY: Repeat bolus twice at 5 min intervals; increase rate to 0.5 ml/kg/min if no recovery.
NOTE: Recovery may take > 1 hour. Propofol is NOT a substitute for Intralipid.
